after.title: Logix and DRI agree CP/M development for Aurelia
after.description: Building on the established DRI partnership, Logix and DRI agree a new CP/M version for Aurelia, fully owned by DRI and available to other vendors. Its development scope includes a text-mode TUI, Plug and Execute smart devices/cards over FlexiBUS, XIP cartridges and names for CP/M User Numbers.

inputs.description: The earlier DRI founding and funding milestone establishes the independent operating-system partner and relationship on which this CP/M collaboration is based.

outcomes.description: The agreed product is a new CP/M version for Logix Aurelia, fully owned by DRI and available for non-exclusive licensing to other vendors. Its scope includes XIP cartridges and named CP/M user areas; implementation and qualification follow this agreement.
The agreement establishes integration of the Logix TUI standard into the CP/M development scope: a consistent pseudo-window user interface in text mode for participating applications.

The agreement establishes CP/M integration work for FlexiBUS smart devices and expansion cards using Plug and Execute. This outcome covers agreed software support, not invention or completed manufacture of the underlying bus.

message: positioning / tagline: Logix Aurelia—a computer like no other. Your personal assistant in business.
positioning / academy message: Learn before you decide.
positioning / audience: Nontechnical business owners and managers; secondary audiences are dealers, software developers and peripheral manufacturers.

positioning / partner message: Business Tools organise office work; Abacus supports planning; independent BPI Systems maintains business records. Logix supplies the computer, not ownership of every application.
tagline: Logix Aurelia—a computer like no other. Your personal assistant in business.
claim_policy: Legacy acceptance wording (not new confirmation) / status: Accepted alternative-story plan; vendor contracts, measured demonstration performance and unspecified operating details remain execution gates.

acceptance gates / 0: Qualify 500-plus-row workload with stated RAM, populated-cell/formula count, IF and fill-down semantics, measured recalculation and disk loading time; sparse storage is not proof of performance.
acceptance gates / 1: Qualify powered-on attachment at quiescent ports, including electrical sequencing and safe suspension of keyboard polling; no unplugging during printing or disk writes.
acceptance gates / 2: Demonstrate save/close/reopen without loss; printer, disk and projection paths must pass the complete rehearsal.
acceptance gates / 3: Confirm celebrity/partner contracts, venue, Academy cities/course dates, tuition, product packages, delivery, warranty and service before publishing definitive claims.
acceptance gates / 4: Measured 48 KB workspace, disk capacity and supported disk configuration; 64 KB or extra drives only when qualified and separately quoted.
acceptance gates / 5: Posting consistency, correction history, disk-full handling and tested backup/restore.
acceptance gates / 6: Readable reports on launch display and supported printers; supported forms and paper documented.
acceptance gates / 7: Payroll jurisdictions, update process and maintenance responsibility explicitly documented.
acceptance gates / 8: Qualify BPI summary export and Abacus import; demonstrate actual sequential applications and label prepared data.

broadcast policy: Every Logix presentation at NCC 1978, including the premiere, both technical sessions, partner appearances, questions and any additional Logix sessions. Offer and supply the material free of charge to any television station wishing to broadcast it; Logix covers normal duplication and dispatch. Supply station-compatible broadcast copies on request.

stage.label: opening
stage.description: Adam introduces almost four years of development toward an accessible, dependable business assistant; acknowledges the assembled personal computers popularised in 1977.

stage.label: reveal
stage.description: Reveal one Aurelia platform with detachable keyboard and two display choices. Power on colour and 16-shade grayscale systems and show startup; no claim of two different CPU models.

stage.label: editing
stage.description: Prepare a customer quotation letter, demonstrate consistent editing and the copy-buffer; explain how learning transfers between applications.

stage.label: peripherals
stage.description: Attach the self-powered printer at a safely quiescent FlexiBUS port with Aurelia powered on, wait for identification, and print. Once the job finishes, safely interchange printer and keyboard ports and verify both. No removal during traffic or unrestricted hot-plug claim.

stage.label: business_tools
stage.description: Use address book, calendar and calculator in the same customer-order workflow.

stage.label: abacus
stage.description: Safely attach external FDD, load Abacus from diskette, explain a small worksheet, then open a 500-plus-row business document. Raise supplier costs by 8%, show automatic recalculation, add and fill a column using IF to flag low-margin orders, print a short report, save, close and reopen. Use readable worksheet sections on 320x200 launch displays. Use a labelled prepared worksheet with BPI-exported totals; explain their origin. The following BPI demonstration shows the source records and export. Rehearse the shorter slot; retain the full workload for hands-on sessions.

stage.label: bpi
stage.description: Independent BPI Systems demonstrates a small wholesaler: existing customer/invoice records, incoming payment and remaining balance, receivables/payables and a concise report, then summary export for Abacus. Prepared history is labelled. No live write-back or simultaneous applications. Software presenter explains the workflow; the BPI head speaks in the subsequent partners section.

stage.label: partners
stage.description: Gary explains independent CP/M OEM availability, published interfaces and optional extensions; CP/M, hardware and application licenses remain distinct. MPI explains the printer partnership and any separately agreed future FlexiBUS devices. Do not announce the later July SMC agreement. The head of BPI Systems explains its independent brand, management, software ownership and support, with Adam investment and AION/Logix cooperation disclosed. No invented name or claim of unrelated ownership.

stage.label: academy
stage.description: Announce Logix Computer Academy in five US cities: learn before you decide, hands-on Fundamentals, configuration advice, 50% tuition purchase credit and direct ordering. Show selected locations, first course dates and exact tuition once finalised. BPI-authorised courses start June 12; specialist support is provided by BPI.

stage.label: packages
stage.description: State complete package contents and prices, delivery dates, warranty, training and service; invite orders, Academy registration and dealer demonstrations; announce the two technical sessions. Show optional dealer-assembled BPI configurations, separate supplier licences and training/setup prices.

stage.label: Aurelia architecture and the open peripheral ecosystem
stage.description: FlexiBUS, display interfaces, implementation/licensing, compatibility and third-party peripheral development.

stage.label: Aurelia C compiler Integrated Development Environment and SDK
stage.description: Build and run an application, common TUI behaviour, published interfaces and C source portability without promising universal binary compatibility.

stage.label: premiere / venue
stage.description: Booked auditorium or negotiated NCC presentation slot in Anaheim; access to a main stage is not assumed.

stage.label: premiere / stages / 7 / description
stage.description: Gary explains independent CP/M OEM availability, published interfaces and optional extensions; CP/M, hardware and application licenses remain distinct. MPI explains the printer partnership and any separately agreed future FlexiBUS devices. Do not announce the later July SMC agreement. The head of BPI Systems explains its independent brand, management, software ownership and support, with AION/Logix cooperation and Adam’s uncompleted investment offer disclosed. No invented name or claim of unrelated ownership.

stage.label: premiere / questions
stage.description: Moderated questions follow the presentation.

stage.label: premiere / display
stage.description: Colour and grayscale launch monitor options; readable 320x200 worksheet sections, not an implied 80-column or whole-document display.

stage.label: technical sessions / 0 / topic
stage.description: Aurelia architecture and the open peripheral ecosystem

stage.label: technical sessions / 1 / topic
stage.description: Aurelia C compiler Integrated Development Environment and SDK

stage.label: business sessions / 0 / provider
stage.description: BPI Systems

stage.label: business sessions / 0 / topic
stage.description: Setup, payments, corrections, backups, month-end, inventory and payroll coverage

marketing_content.description: Proposed 60-second film-trailer-style advertisement; final 10–15 seconds show Aurelia, Abacus, a printed result, logo and June 5 premiere date. Include a recognisable BPI report with its own branding; detailed accounting explanation belongs in print and follow-up films.
Michael Douglas

Narrator introduces This spring. Douglas discusses a remarkably helpful new assistant during a therapy session. The reveal identifies Aurelia as a computer, and the therapist becomes curious about a demonstration.
Warm humour, concrete business benefits and consistent interaction; avoid unhealthy dependency or claims of speech recognition/artificial intelligence.
Telephone enquiries, mailed brochures, demo appointments and Academy bookings; trained staff handle responses.
A modest fraction of an Aurelia package price; publish exact tuition and a named package comparison when commercial prices are selected. Generated pricing proposals are not approved tuition.
Small classes, substantial hands-on time, ideally one machine per participant or pair; business tools, introductory Abacus and advice on appropriate configurations and unnecessary purchases.
Aurelia Fundamentals
Academy direct sales
participating authorised dealers
Logix reimburses participating dealers; do not deduct the credit from their agreed margin.
false
Standalone two-day Fundamentals. Existing $150 vouchers for the other before-you-buy courses remain unchanged; no stacking or extension to other courses is implied.
Reserve the redeemed credit once as promotional expense across the course and computer sale, outside recurring manufacturing costs.
Order and pay at training centres; immediate collection only where stock is available. No purchase obligation.

Access to a BPI specialist at each launch centre; authorised curriculum and escalation agreement. Training, setup and software licensing are separate; no automatic Fundamentals credit for BPI courses.
